items.frozen_body: Minkowski conformal/twistor geometry uses SU(2,2) / Spin(4,2) structure.
A distinguished Euclidean vector can reconstruct an isomorphism between left-handed and conjugate right-handed spinors, relating asymmetric and symmetric descriptions.
The usual Wick rotation of a single Weyl field creates a Euclidean chirality/doubling problem.

The W04a alternative builds spacetime vectors from the right-handed spinor and its conjugate in both signatures, so only SU(2)_R acts geometrically on Euclidean vectors while SU(2)_L is available as an internal symmetry.
items.logical_reading: Build vectors from (right,conjugate-right) in both named signature contexts; role(SU2R,geometric-on-Euclidean-vectors); NOT(role(SU2L,same)); role(SU2L,available-internal).

items.frozen_body: W04c promotes the PT+/PT-/null-orbit holomorphic/boundary picture from an analogy to the proposed fundamental starting point, while stating that a gravitational theory must abandon or deform the global SU(2,2) structure.

In the revised W04c role assignment SL(2,C)_R acts on the twistor CP1 point data while the left factor acts on tangent/quotient data; after the Wick-rotation choice an SU(2)_L role is interpreted internally.
W04c proposes that the choice involved in Wick rotation can break the internal SU(2)_L role, but explicitly says the complete electroweak/Higgs formalism has not been recovered.

W04e applies the same structural proposal in four dimensions: begin with a right-handed holomorphic Euclidean/twistor theory and recover chiral Lorentzian data by a chosen conjugation/real structure instead of adding an independent opposite-chirality Euclidean field.

W01 concludes that the framework is chiral in the gravitational sector as well as the electroweak sector and explicitly leaves open the possibility of observable consequences; this is a source conclusion, not an established prediction.

The proposed right-handed representation gives up the conventional holomorphic SL(2,C)_L x SL(2,C)_R representation used for group-coordinate analytic continuation, while retaining a complex spacetime with real Minkowski and Euclidean subspaces.
